subject: Ignite Health MAP kickoff — POC acceptance criteria & prompt ownership
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@ignitehealth.com>, Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@ignitehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Ignite Health MAP kickoff — POC acceptance criteria & prompt ownership

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I want to formalize the mutual action plan (MAP) kickoff and call out the immediate owners and acceptance gates so everyone is aligned on the 6‑week POC timeline. Attached is a draft MVP benchmark plan and our MAP template for reference.

Key asks in this thread:
- Confirm the Ignite stakeholders who will own clinical acceptance (labels / benchmarks) and procurement contacts for contract timing.
- Confirm a primary technical owner we can loop in on prompt/data access and test data delivery.
- Approve the success criteria below, or suggest edits by EOD Monday.

Draft success criteria (POC acceptance — basic / stretch):
1) Basic acceptance: 3 clinical workflows instrumented, average inference latency <= 350ms p95 on test harness, and >= 85% match rate vs. Ignite human annotation on the primary benchmark set.
2) Stretch: latency <= 250ms p95 with batching enabled, model output matches clinical guidance in >90% of sampled cases across the three workflows.

Proposed owners (Redwood):
- POC lead & MAP steward: Kimberly Park (me) — overall cadence, MAP updates
- Evaluation bench & metrics: Marissa Cole — benchmark design and scoring harness
- Deployment/ops liaison: Rishi Malhotra — runtime config, KV caching, quant profiles
- Sales/contract coordinator: Jordan Blake — procurement and SOW coordination

Tentative timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP owners + procurement timeline
- Week 1: data handoff and bench design sign‑off
- Weeks 2–4: iterative bench runs and prompt tuning; weekly syncs
- Week 5: final acceptance run and executive review
- Week 6: decision (go/no‑go) and next steps (Dedicated or Hosted plan)

I attached the initial bench plan (ignite_mvp_bench_plan.xlsx) and our MAP template. Please reply with Ignite owner names and any edits to the acceptance gates.

Best,

Kimberly Park

Kimberly —

Thanks for pulling this together and for the clear asks. Quick responses inline: 

- Clinical acceptance owner: Dr. Michael Chen (michael.chen@ignitehealth.com, Clinical Ops) will be the clinical lead for annotations and acceptance review.
- Technical owner: Tom Baxter will own ingestion and sandbox access for the POC (he's cc'd).
- Procurement: procurement@ignitehealth.com will handle the SOW and timing; they usually need ~3 weeks for review.

Acceptance criteria look reasonable. A couple of small asks:
1) Can we add a data privacy gate that verifies pseudonymization of PHI fields before bench runs?
2) For the match metric, can Marissa propose the sampling plan & thresholding method so we avoid drift in labeling?

We'll aim to confirm names internally by Monday morning. Tom — can you confirm sandbox readiness and an estimate for dataset delivery?

Appreciate it — looking forward to the kickoff call.

Best,
Elena

Thanks Kim — putting a quick proposal together for the sampling and scoring so we can share with Elena. High level:
- Sampling: stratified by workflow and case complexity (low/med/high); target n=300 per workflow for the acceptance run.
- Scoring: primary metric will be top‑1 clinical match vs. annotation (binary match), secondary will be soft similarity score and false positive rate by tag.
- Stability: we'll measure per‑week drift during tuning phase and set an interim trigger if weekly match drops >5% from baseline.

I'll attach a one‑pager to the MAP doc and add the thresholding math. Rishi — I'll need the test harness format (CSV schema) to wire the scoring.

Marissa

Sandbox is on track. We can deliver a pseudonymized dataset export (approx. 2k records) by Wednesday EOD PT, pending a short data transfer agreement (EDA). Procurement — can you confirm the EDA receiver and a target review date?

- For prompt ownership: Elena, if you agree, we suggest Redwood owns baseline prompt drafts and tuning iterations; Ignite owns final clinical signoff on prompts used for the acceptance run. We'll capture this in the MAP doc.
